string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China and one of its four municipalities administered directly by the central government. The city has a long history as a political centre, including periods as the capital during the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties. Its historic sites include the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and the Summer Palace. Beijing also serves as a centre for education, culture, international exchange and scientific research. Modern neighbourhoods and transport systems sit alongside older streets and courtyards. Mountains surround much of the municipality to the north and west, while its southeastern area extends towards the North China Plain.

Shanghai is a municipality on the eastern coast of China, near the mouth of the Yangtze River. Its location has helped it develop into an important centre for trade, finance and shipping. The Huangpu River runs through the city, separating the historic Bund area from the modern towers of Pudong. Shanghai grew rapidly after opening as a trading port in the nineteenth century. Today, it combines busy commercial districts with older neighbourhoods, museums and gardens. The municipality is part of the Yangtze River Delta and has sixteen administrative districts. Its official flower is the white magnolia, chosen in 1986.

Chongqing is a municipality in southwestern China on the upper reaches of the Yangtze River. Its territory covers about 82,400 square kilometres and includes a large urban centre as well as extensive rural and mountainous areas. It borders Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan and Guizhou. The city centre stands near the meeting of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers, and its steep terrain has shaped its streets, bridges and buildings. Chongqing became a municipality directly under the central government in 1997. It is known for its hotpot, river scenery and role as a transport and industrial centre in western China.

Tianjin is a municipality in northern China near Beijing and the Bohai Sea. The Haihe River runs through its urban area and has played an important part in the development of the city. Tianjin is a major port and an important centre for manufacturing, trade and transport. Its streets contain a mixture of traditional Chinese buildings and architecture connected with its history as a treaty port. The Ancient Culture Street and the Five Great Avenues show different sides of this heritage. The municipality also includes the Binhai New Area, where port facilities and modern industries contribute to its economy.
